TOP: *sshole bug lets attackers into Alpine SSH with no password
LiteLLM release poisoned via a leaked admin key
DigiCert breach exposes business customer data
Claude sandbox probed as agents leak secrets

P.h: *sshole bug lets attackers SSH into some Alpine Linux systems without a password
P.p: TLDR InfoSec says the flaw hits OpenSSH built with musl and without PAM, where an active passwordless account uses SHA256 or SHA512 password hashing. An attacker can send more than 256 characters in the password field and get in with one attempt.
P.s: Alpine and OpenSSH have released patches. Affected systems should update promptly. A separate Hacker News report says Microsoft has fixed an out-of-bounds read in Windows Paint that can enable remote code execution, but Windows Update will not deliver it.

items.h: LiteLLM v1.107.0 attack chain: a committed key was never revoked
items.d: An admin key committed to a public repo on May 27 was removed but not revoked. On October 10 an attacker used it to steal an unscoped GitHub CLI token, override branch protection and publish poisoned wheels and images for about two hours.

items.h: DigiCert breach exposes business customer contact data
items.d: An attacker created a read-only account on an exposed internal archive and accessed data from June 27 to July 2, in some cases identity documents. Certificate-issuing systems were unaffected.

items.h: Iris Ohyama cloud breach exposes 7.7M customers
items.d: A third-party cloud service was breached. Data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and account passwords, which the firm says are encrypted.

items.h: ESXi and Proxmox ransomware needed no VM escape
items.d: Kaspersky GERT cases used reused ESXi root passwords found on a PRTG server and plaintext Proxmox credentials from admin notes. Vault unique per-host credentials.

P.h: AI coding agents leak secrets, write insecure code and get probed
P.p: BishopFox researchers say they got Claude Code to reveal its internals, read its process memory and bypass a local connection block, and found a name-change control could be bypassed through the API. Separately, in tests of nine coding agents, tokens were shared in 15 percent of 181 trials.
P.s: A Qwen benchmark says even the top agent wrote code that was both working and secure only 25.1 percent of the time. TLDR IT adds that Anthropic shipped Claude Enterprise security updates, and UK regulators say firms remain accountable for their AI agents.

tiles.t: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber for authorized security work
tiles.d: Built for vulnerability discovery and patch validation with scope guardrails. Limited to approved Daybreak Red customers.
Thresholds are undisclosed and admins cannot see or override them. Rollout reaches larger firms November 9.

tiles.t: Claude Enterprise adds a security center
tiles.d: Inference hooks for DLP, a parent admin console, remote sign-out and EDR sensor support.
The round is still open and could reach $20 billion. a16z argues defense must move at machine speed: virtual patching and memory-safe code.

items.h: Nvidia opens probe into CEO over reported spy link
items.d: NYT-reported relationship with a woman US agencies see as a Beijing spy. The board says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised.

items.h: Apple pushes Siri toward an autonomous agent
items.d: Bloomberg reports the CEO is pressing software chief Craig Federighi, an AI skeptic, for a bolder strategy.
Lean certificates give confidence, though humans have not validated many AI proofs yet.

items.h: Programming with AI is more tiring
items.d: The repetitive work is automated, leaving higher-judgment tasks. Related: LLMs are poor at designing LLM systems.
